learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will identify Conjunctions and use coordinating (and, but, or) and subordinating (because, although, if) conjunctions to join words and sentences.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Welcome to the grammar construction site! 🚧 Today we are looking at the 'glue' that holds sentences together. Without these sticky words, our sentences would be very short and choppy. Meet the Conjunctions! 🔗

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A Conjunction is a joining word. We use them to connect words, phrases, or short sentences together to make longer, smoother sentences.
examples_or_templates: Sentences: I like cats, BUT my sister likes dogs.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: 'And' joins similar ideas together. 'But' joins opposite or contrasting ideas. 'Or' is used when giving a choice between two things.
examples_or_templates: Addition: We bought apples AND bananas.
Contrast: He is slow, BUT he is steady.
Choice: Will you drink tea OR coffee?

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Some conjunctions explain why things happen or state conditions. 'Because' gives a reason. 'If' states a condition. 'Although' shows surprise or contrast.
examples_or_templates: Reason: She is happy BECAUSE she won.
Condition: We will go to the park IF it stops raining.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Choose the correct conjunction: 'I wanted to buy a toy, _____ I didn't have enough money.'
❓ Which conjunction should be used to combine these sentences? 'He stayed home. He was feeling sick.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Join these two sentences using 'and': 'Rohan is tall. Rohan is strong.'
subjective_practice.hint: You don't need to repeat the name and the verb twice.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with 'although' or 'because': 'We won the match ________ we practiced very hard.'
subjective_practice.hint: Does the second part give a reason, or does it show a surprise?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Finish the sentence: 'You can watch TV if ________.'
subjective_practice.hint: Add a condition that must be completed first.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🚂 The Sentence Train
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write one short, simple sentence (e.g., 'I woke up early'). Now, use three different conjunctions to make three completely different long sentences out of it! (e.g., I woke up early AND... / I woke up early BUT... / I woke up early BECAUSE...)

chapter_summary: ⭐ Conjunctions are joining words that connect words, phrases, or sentences.
⭐ 'And' adds information, 'but' shows contrast, and 'or' gives a choice.
⭐ Words like 'because', 'although', and 'if' connect a reason or condition to the main sentence.
